## PART A — whatsapp-web.js

- **What it is:** WhatsApp client library for Node.js that drives a real headless Chromium instance of WhatsApp Web via **Puppeteer** (runs an actual browser, not a raw protocol client). [github.com/pedroslopez/whatsapp-web.js](https://github.com/pedroslopez/whatsapp-web.js)
- **Stars / scale:** ~**22.2k** GitHub stars; **124 releases** documented. [repo](https://github.com/pedroslopez/whatsapp-web.js)
- **Latest release:** **v1.34.7, released April 24 2026** — actively maintained (PRs merged within days as of July 2026: media uploads, call handling, marked-unread fixes). [releases](https://github.com/pedroslopez/whatsapp-web.js/releases)
- **Linking — QR code:** Primary method. `client.on('qr', ...)` renders a QR you scan from the phone's Linked Devices. [repo](https://github.com/pedroslopez/whatsapp-web.js)
- **Linking — pairing code: YES, supported.** Set `pairWithPhoneNumber` in the Client constructor (phoneNumber in international symbol-free format, `showNotification`, `intervalMs`) and listen to the `'code'` event. Maps to WhatsApp's "Link with phone number" feature — no QR needed. Gotcha: calling `requestPairingCode()` from the `'qr'` event fails silently; phone-number pairing can hit **429 rate limits** (`IQErrorRateOverlimit`). [PR #3180](https://github.com/pedroslopez/whatsapp-web.js/pull/3180) · [issue #3763](https://github.com/wwebjs/whatsapp-web.js/issues/3763)
- **Linked-device / same-account behavior: CONFIRMED.** Multi-Device is a supported feature (✅ in the matrix). It links as a **companion device sharing the same WhatsApp account** — messages the agent sends/receives appear on that account's phone app. This is exactly the same linked-device model as Baileys. [repo](https://github.com/pedroslopez/whatsapp-web.js)
- **Group support: FULL.** Add/remove participants, promote/demote admins, modify group settings, send/receive in groups — unlike the official Cloud API which is template/session-constrained. [repo](https://github.com/pedroslopez/whatsapp-web.js)
- **Tradeoffs vs Baileys:**
  - **Resource:** whatsapp-web.js = a Chromium process **per session, hundreds of MB (~0.5 GB) RAM each**; Baileys = raw WebSocket protocol client, **~50 MB RAM, sub-second startup, no Chromium**. Baileys scales to many numbers per box far more cheaply. [wasphere.com](https://wasphere.com/blog/open-source-whatsapp-api-landscape-2026/) · [buildmvpfast.com](https://www.buildmvpfast.com/blog/whatsapp-ai-agent-open-source-self-hosted-api-2026)
  - **API ergonomics:** whatsapp-web.js is "batteries-included," simpler API; Baileys is lighter but lower-level.
  - **ToS / ban risk: identical and real.** Both are unofficial, both violate WhatsApp ToS, both can get the linked number **permanently banned without warning**. Reported unofficial-client lifespans ~2–8 weeks before detection in aggressive-use scenarios; the repo itself warns it "shouldn't be considered totally safe." [checkleaked.cc](https://whatsapp.checkleaked.cc/blog/whatsapp-cloud-api-vs-unofficial) · [kraya-ai.com](https://blog.kraya-ai.com/whatsapp-automation-ban-risk)
  - **Verdict from sources:** pick Baileys for lightweight/many-number/browser-free; pick whatsapp-web.js for a simple all-in-one API when the Chromium overhead is acceptable.

## PART B — dedicated number that can actually register for WhatsApp

- **The isolation pattern (confirmed sound):** because a linked device shares the owner's account, the only way to keep the agent's chats **out of the owner's personal WhatsApp** is to register a **separate, dedicated number that the agent owns** — then link the library to *that* account. A second physical SIM/eSIM or a working virtual number.
- **WhatsApp now actively rejects VoIP ranges.** Platforms run **number-intelligence lookups** (Twilio Lookup, Ekata, NumVerify) that classify carrier type; anything returning `fixedVoip`/`nonFixedVoip` is refused at verification. WhatsApp, Google, Discord all reject VoIP as of 2026. [dev.to/fathin_dosunmu](https://dev.to/fathin_dosunmu/why-your-ai-agents-phone-number-gets-blocked-and-how-to-fix-it-48k5) · [multilogin.com](https://multilogin.com/blog/best-non-voip-phone-numbers-sms-verification/)
- **Google Voice: REJECTED** by WhatsApp verification (blocked). [multilogin.com](https://multilogin.com/blog/best-non-voip-phone-numbers-sms-verification/)
- **TextNow: REJECTED** — blocked by WhatsApp since ~2024 in most cases. [multilogin.com](https://multilogin.com/blog/best-non-voip-phone-numbers-sms-verification/)
- **Twilio — the important nuance:**
  - Twilio does **NOT** give you a personal-style number to register the consumer WhatsApp app. Twilio's WhatsApp offering is the **official WhatsApp Business/Cloud API sender** (you enable a Twilio number *as* a Business API sender), which is a different product from linking whatsapp-web.js/Baileys to a personal account.
  - For enabling a Twilio number on WhatsApp Business, success is **number-type dependent** — non-US toll-free and certain types have "mixed success rates"; Twilio itself recommends a different number type. Toll-free needs paid account + toll-free verification. [Twilio Help](https://help.twilio.com/articles/360026678054) · [Twilio toll-free guide](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/developer-guide-to-toll-free-verification)
  - Bottom line: Twilio is the path if you go **official Cloud API** (no groups, template rules), **not** for verifying a personal-account number to drive with an unofficial library.
- **Airalo / travel eSIMs: WON'T work as the verification number.** Airalo packs are **data-only, no phone number, cannot receive SMS or voice** — so they can't receive the WhatsApp verification code. They only let you *use* an already-registered WhatsApp over data. Not a source of a dedicated registerable number. [Airalo Help](https://www.airalo.com/help/using-managing-esims/ZSEEHBT5HW6F/can-i-make-phone-calls-or-send-sms-with-my-esim/V9CFOOQYA2DU) · [airalo.com/blog](https://www.airalo.com/blog/are-esims-attached-to-numbers)
- **What RELIABLY works in 2026:**
  1. **A real physical SIM/eSIM from an actual mobile carrier** (AT&T/Verizon/T-Mobile, or any local prepaid carrier SIM). Passes every carrier lookup, **90–99% verification success** — the most reliable, and it gives the agent a genuine dedicated line. This is the recommended isolation approach. [multilogin.com](https://multilogin.com/blog/best-non-voip-phone-numbers-sms-verification/)
  2. **Paid single-use SMS-verification services that specifically advertise WhatsApp** and route real mobile (non-VoIP) numbers: **SMS-Activate** ($0.07–$3/number), **5SIM** (WhatsApp listed, 85–95% success), **SMSPVA** ($0.10–$1). These pass WhatsApp's aggressive VoIP detection — but the number is often rented/temporary, a risk if you need to keep the account long-term (re-verification later may fail). [multilogin.com](https://multilogin.com/blog/best-non-voip-phone-numbers-sms-verification/) · [voidmob.com](https://voidmob.com/blog/best-non-voip-sms-verification-services-2026)
- **The reliable answer:** for a *persistent* dedicated agent line, use a **real prepaid carrier SIM/eSIM you keep** — that is the dependable, ownable, isolation-clean option. VoIP (Google Voice/TextNow) is out; Twilio is a different (official-API) product; travel data eSIMs (Airalo) can't receive the code. SMS-Activate/5SIM/SMSPVA work for one-shot verification but are rented numbers, weaker for a long-lived account.
